info.title: Keasy API
info.description: Keasy host: identity, connections, signed URLs and the job record

get.summary:
The providers an ask can run on, and the model each runs when its settings
name none. Whether one is configured is `/v1/settings/ai/providers`.

200.description: Every provider keasy can call, with its default model
SSE stream: delta events + complete with GenerateResponse
SSE stream: delta events + complete with SuggestResponse

get.description:
The one thing the web cannot answer from its own session: the switcher's
list. `Session` carries who you are and what you may do, and the workspaces
claim is neither — so it is read here, off the token this server verified,
rather than copied into a shape the browser would have to be trusted about.

It takes no role extractor: someone authenticated but
holding no role here still needs to be told where they *do* belong.

400.description: Invalid connection or container not found

get.summary:
The connections a program may read, by the name it writes after `@`. No
credentials: signing is [`sign_locators`].

200.description: Every source connection's base URL, by name

post.summary:
Sign GET URLs for locators, each with the credentials of the connection it
lies under. Serves the editor and a job's run alike: a member reads what
every source connection holds, and the sink only through the job that
wrote it. Public HTTP locators come back as they are.

200.description: Signed GET URLs for the locators the caller may read
List of files in the connection

get.summary:
Every dataset the workspace produced, as the corpus reader named it: the
owner's index over the whole workspace. It carries metadata only; the
member reaches the bytes through the job that made them.

400.description: The destination is not a sink

patch.summary:
The browser ran the mapping and uploaded the output; this records the
outcome. `Completed` stores the run report verbatim, unread.

200.description: Job status updated from the browser run

post.summary:
Sign GET URLs so the browser reads the dataset directly — the reading twin of
[`resolve_output_urls`]. It takes the list the corpus reader enumerated and
derives none.

200.description: Signed GET URLs for the requested dataset keys

400.description: The destination connection is gone, or a path outside the dataset

post.summary:
Sign PUT URLs so the browser uploads the output it just produced straight to
the job's sink.

200.description: Signed PUT URLs for the output keys

400.description: The destination connection is gone, or a path outside the dataset

put.summary:
What the corpus reader found: the relations a finished job's output holds,
their names and the files that carry them, as `@fossil-lang/corpus`
enumerated them in the browser.
put.description:
It is a second call and not a field of the completion because naming a
relation is an answer only a reader holding the manifests can give, and the
run report is not that reader. keasy stores the answer verbatim; it is what
the owner's datasets view lists.

400.description: A file path outside the dataset

AiProvider.description: An LLM provider keasy can call.

AiProviderInfo.description: A provider keasy can call, and the model it runs when none is configured.

AiSettingsPayload.description:
A configured provider as the settings page shows it: the key is only ever
said to be there.

api_key.description: `"••••"` when a key is stored, empty otherwise.

explain.description:
When true, the model reads query results back instead of writing SQL;
`question` then carries the question, the SQL and the rows.

history.description: The conversation so far, oldest first.

schema.description:
DuckDB DDL of the views the browser mounted: the whole of what the model
knows about the data. Required unless `explain`.

CatalogStoragePayload.description: The workspace write sink, as the owner's Catalog Storage page edits it.

ChatMessage.description:
One earlier message of the conversation. The client keeps the conversation;
the server sees only what each ask carries.

ColumnInfo.description: A source column as the browser described it.

CompleteJobRequest.description:
The browser-driven completion payload (PATCH `/v1/jobs/{id}`): after running
the mapping in the browser (`@fossil-lang/executor`) and uploading the output
by signed PUT, the client reports the run's outcome. `manifest` is the
executor's run report, stored verbatim and never read.

manifest.description: The run report for the uploaded output (on `Completed`) — opaque JSON.

status.description: The terminal (or `Running`) status the client is transitioning the job to.

direction.description: Read source vs the workspace write sink. Defaults to `source`.

refs.description: Source connection name → base URL, the map `@name/…` expands against.

CreateCloudAccountRequest.description:
Every field value arrives as a secret: which of them are credentials is the
provider schema's to say, and until it has, none is logged or printed.

direction.description: `source` (default) or `sink` (the owner output store; one per workspace).

sink_connection_id.description: Where the output lands: a sink connection.

Dataset.description: A completed job's output, as the owner's datasets view lists it.

paths.description:
Paths relative to the dataset (or connection). The caller names them —
the executor's output, the corpus reader's enumeration — and keasy signs
the list it is handed.

Direction.description:
Whether a connection is a READ source (programs reference it via `@conn`) or
the workspace's WRITE sink (where the owner's job output is materialised).
Orthogonal to [`ConnectionKind`] (which describes a source's data) and
[`LocationType`]: a connection is a named, credentialed storage location, and
`direction` says how it is used. Exactly one `sink` exists per workspace (the
owner output store); `kind` is source-only and ignored for a sink.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every 4xx/5xx, and the payload of an SSE `error` frame.

ErrorCode.description:
Every error the server answers with. Closed: a code the server does not
declare here cannot be sent, and the web keys its copy by this enum.

FileEntry.description: One object under a connection's prefix.

created_by.description:
Keycloak `sub` of the member who created the job, and the only one who
may see, change, run or read it. Taken from the token, never the body.

error.description: Why a `Failed` run failed, as the browser that ran it reported it.

manifest.description:
What the run reported, verbatim and **opaque**: fossil's own run report,
which IS the manifest the corpus carries. keasy stores it, hands it back
and never reads a field of it — the last time a host re-typed this
struct, it ended up asking for `vertex/<Type>.parquet`, a file the
layout pass deletes. Its presence is the one thing keasy asks of it:
"this job produced output".

relations.description:
What the corpus holds and what it is called, as the corpus reader
enumerated it (`@fossil-lang/corpus`). fossil names every relation and
every file; keasy joins them to the destination it owns and signs them
for reading.

sink_connection_id.description:
The sink the output lands in, under `{sink.url}/{job_id}`, signed with
that connection's credentials.

OutputRelation.description:
One addressable relation of a job's output, named by fossil.

`name` is the relation the corpus registers and queries by (`Person`,
`Person_knows_Person`) — **keasy does not compose it**; it is what the
corpus reader answered. `files` are the dataset-relative payload files the
corpus addressing enumerated, `rows` the count it reported and `columns`
what a row carries.

PublishRelationsRequest.description:
What the corpus reader enumerated for a finished job (PUT
`/v1/jobs/{id}/relations`). It arrives after completion because naming a
relation is the corpus's answer, not the report's: only a reader with the
manifests in hand can say what the dataset is called and which files carry
it.

data_type.description: The engine's spelling of the Parquet type (`VARCHAR`, `BIGINT`, …).

urls.description: Locator → fetchable URL. A locator keasy will not sign is absent.

fields.description: An empty secret keeps the stored one.

VersionResponse.description:
The running build's version, so an operator can see which image a tenant is
on. `git_sha`/`built_at` are stamped at build time (CI sets `KEASY_GIT_SHA`/
`KEASY_BUILT_AT`); `version` is the crate version.

current.description: This instance's slug — the "current" entry in the switcher.

current_name.description:
This instance's display name (`KEASY_WORKSPACE_NAME`). The other
entries show their slug: an instance only knows its own name.

workspaces.description:
Slugs of every workspace the user belongs to, read from the `workspaces`
claim on the token this request carried. The web builds each
`<slug>.<domain>` link.

Forbidden.description: The caller holds no role this route admits

KeysUnavailable.description: The identity provider's keys are unreachable

RateLimited.description: The caller exceeded their request rate
